question:
The sentence given below contains some spelling errors. Select the option that has the correct spellings.

Memberrs of the asocciation have succesfully climbed several paeks of the Himalayan range.
option_1: Members of the associattion have succesfully climbed several paeks of the Himalayan range.
option_2: Meembers of the associatiion have successfuly climbed several peaks of the Himalayan range.
option_3: Members of the associasion have succesfully climbed several paiks of the Himalayan range.
option_4: Members of the association have successfully climbed several peaks of the Himalayan range.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Members of the association have successfully climbed several peaks of the Himalayan range.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence contains four misspelt words — "Memberrs", "asocciation", "succesfully" and "paeks". Only Option 4 corrects all four of them at the same time.

◦ Memberrs → Members (MEM + BERS; only one "r").

◦ asocciation → association (AS + SO + CI + A + TION; double "s", single "c").

◦ succesfully → successfully (SUC + CESS + FUL + LY; double "c", double "s", single "l" in "-ful" + "-ly").

◦ paeks → peaks (PEAK = the pointed top of a mountain).

• Correct sentence: Members of the association have successfully climbed several peaks of the Himalayan range.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 still keeps "associattion", "succesfully" and "paeks" wrong.

• Option 2 keeps "Meembers", "associatiion" and "successfuly" wrong.

• Option 3 keeps "associasion", "succesfully" and "paiks" wrong.

NOTE

• Useful meanings: association (संघ/संस्था) = an organised group of people; peak (शिखर) = the top of a mountain; successfully (सफलतापूर्वक) = in a way that achieves the desired result.

• Do not confuse peak (mountain top), peek (a quick look) and pique (to annoy / arouse interest).

question: Choose the sentence that contains an error.
option_1: The Mona Lisa is a famous painting by Leonardo da Vinci.
option_2: She is the only person who can speak five languages fluently.
option_3: He is a doctor who specialises in the treating rare diseases.
option_4: I saw the movie that won the Academy Award for Best Picture.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. He is a doctor who specialises in the treating rare diseases.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The article "the" is wrongly placed before the gerund "treating". When a gerund is followed directly by its object ("rare diseases"), it does not take an article.

◦ Incorrect: He is a doctor who specialises in the treating rare diseases.

◦ Correct: He is a doctor who specialises in treating rare diseases. (or — "in the treatment of rare diseases")

• "Specialise in + V-ing" is the fixed structure.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is correct — "The Mona Lisa" is a specific painting, so "the" is right, and "by Leonardo da Vinci" shows the agent.

• Option 2 is correct — "the only person who" uses the correct relative pronoun for a person, and "fluently" (adverb) correctly modifies "speak".

• Option 4 is correct — "the movie that won" uses a proper defining relative clause.

NOTE

• Rule for gerunds: "the" + gerund + "of" + object ("the treating of rare diseases") OR bare gerund + object ("treating rare diseases"). Mixing the two — "the treating rare diseases" — is always wrong.

• Similar: "in the writing of letters" / "in writing letters" (both fine), but NOT "in the writing letters".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a spelling error.

The conferrence / attempts to / trace the processes and / consequences of climate change.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The conferrence.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Conferrence" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "conference" — a formal meeting for discussion. (सम्मेलन)

◦ Spelling key: CON + FER + ENCE — only one "r".

◦ Correct: The conference attempts to trace the processes and consequences of climate change.

• Learners often double the "r" by analogy with "referred/preferred", but in "conference" the stress shifts to the first syllable, so the "r" is not doubled.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "attempts to", "trace the processes and" and "consequences of climate change" are all correctly spelt.

• "consequences" (परिणाम) = results or effects; "processes" (प्रक्रियाएँ) = a series of actions or steps.

NOTE

• Same family: confer (to discuss / to award), conferred, conferring — these DO double the "r" — but the noun conference does not.

• Other commonly misspelt "-ence" words: occurrence (double r and double c), preference, existence, persistence, independence.

question:
Select the word segment which substitutes the bracketed word correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully.

Mathematics (are not) easy to learn.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. is not.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mathematics" is a subject name. Although it ends in "-s", it is treated as a singular uncountable noun and therefore takes a singular verb.

◦ Correct: Mathematics is not easy to learn.

• The sentence states a general/universal truth, so the simple present tense ("is") is required, not the past ("was"/"were").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "were not" (plural + past) and 2 "was not" (past) wrongly shift the tense to the past.

• Option 3 "has not" is grammatically impossible before the adjective "easy" — "has not easy" is not a valid structure.

NOTE

• Nouns ending in -ics that take a singular verb: mathematics, physics, economics, politics, statistics, civics, ethics, athletics, news, measles, mumps.

◦ Example: "Physics is my favourite subject." / "The news is disturbing."

• But when "statistics/politics" mean "figures/opinions" rather than the subject, they take a plural verb: "The statistics are misleading."

• Nouns that are always plural: scissors, trousers, spectacles, tongs, pincers, cattle, police.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The action of formally accusing a public official of a serious offence
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Impeachment.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Impeachment" means the act of formally charging/accusing a public official (such as a President or a judge) with a serious offence or misconduct, usually before a legislature. (महाभियोग)

◦ Example: The impeachment motion against the judge was moved in Parliament.

• The key words in the definition — "formally", "public official" and "serious offence" — point exactly to impeachment.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Condemnation" (निंदा) = strong disapproval or a sentence of punishment — it is not a formal charge against an official.

• Option 3 "Summon" (समन/बुलाना) = to order someone to appear (in a court) — it is not an accusation of an offence.

• Option 4 "Allegation" (आरोप) = a claim that someone has done something wrong, made without proof and not necessarily formal or against a public official.

NOTE

• Static-GK link useful for SSC: in India, the President can be removed by impeachment under Article 61 for "violation of the Constitution", while judges of the Supreme Court/High Courts are removed by a motion under Articles 124(4)/217.

• Related one-word substitutes: indictment (a formal criminal charge), arraignment (bringing an accused before a court), acquittal (a declaration of innocence).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A number which is used to divide another number
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Divisor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "divisor" is the number by which another number (the dividend) is divided. (भाजक)

◦ Example: In 20 ÷ 4 = 5, the number 4 is the divisor, 20 is the dividend and 5 is the quotient.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Divisible" is an adjective (capable of being divided without a remainder), not a noun naming a number.

• Option 2 "Quotient" (भागफल) is the result obtained on dividing.

• Option 3 "Remainder" (शेषफल) is what is left over when the division is not exact.

NOTE

• The division algorithm, useful in SSC Maths: Dividend = Divisor × Quotient + Remainder.

◦ Example: 23 = 4 × 5 + 3, where divisor = 4, quotient = 5, remainder = 3.

• Related terms: HCF (Highest Common Factor) is the greatest common divisor; factor is a divisor that leaves no remainder.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To cut someone some slack
option_1: Avoid talking about problems till the very end
option_4: To not manage someone very strictly or critically
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To not manage someone very strictly or critically.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to cut someone some slack" means to be less strict or critical with someone; to allow them extra freedom or make allowances for them. (किसी के प्रति नरमी बरतना / रियायत देना)

◦ Example: He has just lost his father, so cut him some slack about the late submission.

• The image comes from loosening a rope ("slack" = the loose part of a rope) — i.e., not keeping someone on a tight leash.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes beating about the bush / putting off, not this idiom.

• Option 2 describes "breaking the ice".

• Option 3 is the exact opposite — being strict is "to be hard on someone" or "to keep someone on a tight rein".

NOTE

• Similar idioms of leniency: "give someone the benefit of the doubt", "go easy on someone", "let someone off the hook", "turn a blind eye".

• Opposite idioms: "come down hard on someone", "take someone to task", "crack the whip".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

Our trainer asked for _______ on her for the next informative session.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. all eyes and ears.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "all eyes and ears" means to be giving one's full attention; to watch and listen very carefully. (पूरा ध्यान देना / पूरी तरह सजग रहना)

◦ Correct: Our trainer asked for all eyes and ears on her for the next informative session.

• The context — a trainer starting an informative session — clearly calls for the audience's complete attention, so this idiom fits perfectly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "chasing rainbows" = pursuing something impossible or unrealistic.

• Option 2 "(a)round the bend" = mad, crazy, out of one's mind.

• Option 4 "going bananas" = becoming very excited, angry or crazy.

• None of these three suits a request for attention.

NOTE

• Related attention idioms: "be all ears" (listening eagerly), "keep an eye on" (to watch), "pay heed to", "hang on someone's every word", "glued to".

• Opposite ideas: "turn a deaf ear" (to ignore), "in one ear and out the other".

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

Children below the age of 14 were not allowed to partisipate in the cooking competition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Partisipate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Partisipate" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "participate", meaning to take part in something. (भाग लेना)

◦ Spelling key: PAR + TI + CI + PATE — the third syllable is written with a "c", not an "s", even though it is pronounced /s/.

◦ Correct: Children below the age of 14 were not allowed to participate in the cooking competition.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Competition", "Children" and "Allowed" are all correctly spelt in the sentence.

• Word family: participate (verb), participation (noun — भागीदारी), participant (noun — a person who takes part), participatory (adjective).

NOTE

• The soft "c" (pronounced /s/) appears in many exam words: participate, decide, necessary, medicine, receive, precede, exercise, sincere. Learn them by the spelling, not the sound.

• Other frequently misspelt SSC words: accommodation, occurrence, embarrass, questionnaire, maintenance, definitely, separate, privilege.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After I complete my training program / I will have been joining a team of astronauts / and preparing to / embark on a mission to Mars.
option_1: I will have been joining a team of astronauts
option_2: embark on a mission to Mars
option_4: After I complete my training program
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. I will have been joining a team of astronauts.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Will have been joining" (future perfect continuous) is wrong here. "Join" denotes a single, completed action at a point of time, not an action stretching over a period, so the simple future "will be joining / will join" is required.

◦ Correct: After I complete my training program, I will be joining a team of astronauts and preparing to embark on a mission to Mars.

• The parallel structure with "and preparing to" also demands "will be joining ... and preparing to ..." — a future continuous in both limbs.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 4 "After I complete my training program" is correct — in a time clause beginning with "after/when/before/until", we use the present simple for a future meaning, never "will".

• Segment 3 "and preparing to" and Segment 2 "embark on a mission to Mars" are both correct ("embark on" = to begin/set out on).

NOTE

• Future tense forms: Simple future (will + V1), Future continuous (will be + V-ing), Future perfect (will have + V3), Future perfect continuous (will have been + V-ing + since/for).

• The future perfect continuous normally needs a duration marker — "By 2030, I will have been working here for ten years." Without such a marker, as in this sentence, it is unnatural.

question:
The given sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the bad.
option_1: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.
option_2: Earlier, he was feeling good, but things took a turn for the bad.
option_3: Earlier, he was feeling well, but things took a turn for the ill.
option_4: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the ill.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To take a turn for the worst" / "a turn for the worse" is a fixed idiomatic expression meaning to start becoming worse; to deteriorate suddenly. The expression never uses "bad" or "ill".

◦ Correct: Earlier, he was feeling better, but things took a turn for the worst.

• The contrast marker "but" signals a change from improvement ("feeling better") to deterioration, which "for the worst" conveys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 keeps the wrong phrase "a turn for the bad" and needlessly changes "better" to "good".

• Options 3 and 4 use "a turn for the ill", which is not an English idiom at all.

• The opposite idiom is "to take a turn for the better" — to start improving.

NOTE

• Degrees: bad – worse – worst. In fixed idioms, learn the form as a chunk: "at worst", "if worse comes to worst", "a change for the better".

• Health usage: "he is feeling better" (comparative — improving) and "he is well" (adjective of health) are both correct English; the error in this sentence lies only in the idiom.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Blessing in disguise
option_1: Something that seems good but is harmful for you
option_2: Something that seems bad but provides some benefit
option_3: Something that cannot be hidden from anyone
option_4: Something that remains hidden from everyone
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Something that seems bad but provides some benefit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a blessing in disguise" means a misfortune that unexpectedly turns out to be a good thing; something that appears bad at first but eventually proves beneficial. (छिपा हुआ वरदान)

◦ Example: Missing that flight was a blessing in disguise — the plane was delayed for nine hours.

• "Disguise" = a changed appearance that hides the true nature; hence the "blessing" is hidden behind an apparently bad event.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes the opposite idea — a "wolf in sheep's clothing" or a "poisoned chalice".

• Options 3 and 4 talk about hiding/exposure and correspond to expressions such as "an open secret" or "under wraps", not to this idiom.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "every cloud has a silver lining", "a blessing in the making", "good comes out of evil".

• Contrasting idioms: "a wolf in sheep's clothing" (a danger disguised as something harmless), "fair-weather friend", "all that glitters is not gold".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Break
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Mend.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Break" means to separate into pieces; to damage or destroy. (तोड़ना)

• Its antonym is "Mend", which means to repair something that is broken or damaged. (मरम्मत करना / जोड़ना)

◦ Example: The child broke the toy and his father mended it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Divide" (to separate into parts) is close in sense to break — a synonym, not an antonym.

• Option 3 "Split" (to break/cut into parts) is a synonym of break.

• Option 4 "Breach" (to break through a wall or to violate an agreement) is also a synonym/related word.

NOTE

• Synonyms of break: shatter, smash, fracture, crack, snap, rupture, split, breach.

• Antonyms of break: mend, repair, fix, join, unite, restore, patch up.

• Useful idiom: "Least said, soonest mended" — the less you say, the sooner a quarrel is repaired.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A place of burial
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cemetery.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cemetery" is a place/ground where dead bodies are buried. (कब्रिस्तान / समाधिस्थल)

◦ Example: The soldiers were laid to rest in the war cemetery.

• Spelling key: CE + ME + TERY — all three vowels are "e" (a very common SSC spelling trap; "cemetary" is wrong).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Building" is a general structure, not specifically a burial place.

• Option 2 "Laboratory" is a place for scientific experiments.

• Option 4 "Observatory" is a place for observing stars, planets and the weather.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes frequently asked in SSC exams:

◦ Graveyard / Churchyard — a burial ground attached to a church.

◦ Crematorium — a place where dead bodies are burnt (श्मशान).

◦ Mausoleum — a large, stately tomb (e.g., the Taj Mahal).

◦ Epitaph — words written on a tombstone.

◦ Obituary — a notice of a person's death in a newspaper.

◦ Sepulchre — a tomb cut in rock or built of stone.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Forthcoming
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Past.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Forthcoming" means about to happen or appear in the near future; approaching. (आगामी / आने वाला)

◦ Example: Details of the forthcoming examination will be published soon.

• Its antonym is "Past", which refers to the time that has already gone by. (बीता हुआ)

◦ Example: Past events cannot be changed, but forthcoming ones can be planned.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Large" and Option 2 "Extensive" relate to size/extent, not to time.

• Option 3 "Adventurous" relates to daring behaviour, and is unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of forthcoming: upcoming, approaching, imminent, impending, prospective, future, ensuing.

• Antonyms of forthcoming: past, bygone, previous, former, elapsed.

• "Forthcoming" has a second meaning — willing to give information; communicative ("The witness was not very forthcoming"); its antonym in that sense is reticent/secretive.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

I will celebrating New Year at my old residence as usual.
option_4: at my old residence as usual.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. will celebrating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal auxiliary "will", we must use the base form (V1) of the verb, or the full future continuous structure "will be + V-ing". "will celebrating" is missing the helping verb "be".

◦ Correct: I will be celebrating New Year at my old residence as usual.

◦ Also correct: I will celebrate New Year at my old residence as usual.

• The phrase "as usual" indicates a habitual future arrangement, so "will be celebrating" is the most natural correction.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "I" is the correct subject pronoun.

• Segment 3 "New Year" is a proper noun and rightly capitalised, with no article needed.

• Segment 4 "at my old residence as usual." uses the correct preposition "at" with a specific place.

NOTE

• Modals (will, shall, can, could, may, might, must, should, would) are always followed by the bare infinitive (V1) — "will go", "must write", "can swim".

• Future continuous = will/shall be + V-ing; it describes an action that will be in progress at a future time, or a planned/expected future event.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.

Why don’t / you throw this / paper on the dust bin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. paper on the dust bin.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The preposition "on" is wrong. Something thrown inside a container takes "in / into", not "on" (which means resting on top of a surface).

◦ Correct: Why don't you throw this paper in / into the dust bin?

• "Into" stresses the movement from outside to inside, which suits the verb "throw".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment "Why don't" is a correct negative interrogative used for a suggestion.

• Segment "you throw this" is correct — after "Why don't", the base form of the verb ("throw") is used.

• Since a clear error exists, Option 2 "No error" cannot be chosen.

NOTE

• Prepositions of place: in/into (inside something — in the box, into the room), on/onto (on a surface — on the table), at (a point — at the door).

• Verbs of motion normally take into/onto: "jump into the pool", "climb onto the roof", "put the letter into the envelope".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Beat around the bush
option_1: To be persistent in pursuing a goal
option_4: To avoid addressing a topic correctly
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. To avoid addressing a topic correctly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to beat around (about) the bush" means to avoid coming to the main point; to talk in a roundabout way instead of dealing with the topic directly. (इधर-उधर की बात करना / मुद्दे पर न आना)

◦ Example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me how much you need.

• Its origin lies in hunting — beaters struck the bushes around the game instead of going straight for it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 describes "stick to one's guns" / "keep at it".

• Option 2 describes "have a short fuse" / "fly off the handle".

• Option 3 is the exact opposite — being direct is "to come straight to the point" or "to call a spade a spade".

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "mince words" (to soften what one says), "hedge", "skirt an issue", "talk in circles".

• Opposite idioms: "get down to brass tacks", "cut to the chase", "come to the point", "call a spade a spade".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Her stories paid _____ to her mother, whom she regarded as the goddess of bravery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. homage.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To pay homage (to someone)" is a fixed collocation meaning to show great respect, honour or reverence to someone. (श्रद्धांजलि अर्पित करना / सम्मान देना)

◦ Correct: Her stories paid homage to her mother, whom she regarded as the goddess of bravery.

• The clause "whom she regarded as the goddess of bravery" clearly shows admiration and respect, which only "homage" expresses.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "frustration" (निराशा) = a feeling of annoyance at being unable to do something — the opposite mood.

• Option 2 "sainthood" = the state of being a saint; one cannot "pay sainthood".

• Option 3 "absoluteness" = the quality of being complete/unconditional — it does not collocate with "pay".

NOTE

• Common "pay" collocations: pay homage/tribute/respect/attention/a visit/a compliment/heed.

• Synonyms of homage: tribute, reverence, respect, honour, veneration. Antonyms: contempt, disrespect, dishonour.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Amicable
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Friendly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Amicable" means characterised by friendliness and goodwill; peaceable and without quarrelling. (मैत्रीपूर्ण / सौहार्दपूर्ण)

◦ Example: The two countries reached an amicable settlement of the border dispute.

• Its closest synonym among the options is "Friendly".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Proud" (गर्वित) refers to self-respect or arrogance, not friendliness.

• Option 3 "Generous" (उदार) means willing to give — a different quality.

• Option 4 "Harsh" (कठोर) is an antonym of amicable.

NOTE

• Synonyms of amicable: friendly, cordial, congenial, harmonious, peaceable, good-natured, amiable.

• Antonyms of amicable: hostile, unfriendly, antagonistic, belligerent, harsh, acrimonious.

• Note the difference: amicable describes relations/settlements ("an amicable divorce"), while amiable describes people ("an amiable host").

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Once, there was a boy who became bored when he watched over the village sheep (1)________ on the hillside. To entertain himself, he sang out, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers heard the cry, they came (2)________ the hill to drive the wolf away. But, when they arrived, they saw no wolf. The boy was amused when seeing their angry faces. “Don’t scream wolf, boy,” warned the villagers, “when there is no wolf!” They angrily went back down the hill. Later, the shepherd boy cried out once again, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers came, they saw there was no wolf, they said strictly, “Save your (3)________ cry for when there is really a wolf! Don’t cry ‘wolf’ when there is no wolf!” Later, the boy saw a real wolf sneaking around his flock. Alarmed, he jumped on his feet and cried out as loud as he could, “Wolf! Wolf!” But the villagers thought he was (4)________ them again, and so they didn’t come to help. At sunset, the villagers went looking for the boy who hadn’t returned with their sheep. When they went up the hill, they found him (5)________ as all the sheep were dead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. grazing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Grazing" means (of animals) feeding on growing grass in a field or on a hillside. (चरना)

◦ Correct: ... he watched over the village sheep grazing on the hillside.

• The subject of the blank is "the village sheep" and the place is "on the hillside", so the only natural activity is grazing. The boy's job was to watch over the sheep while they fed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "laughing" cannot be done by sheep.

• Option 2 "receiving" needs an object (receiving *what*?) and makes no sense here.

• Option 3 "assisting" (helping) also needs an object and does not fit sheep on a hillside.

NOTE

• Vocabulary from the passage: flock (a group of sheep), shepherd (one who tends sheep — गड़रिया), pasture (grassland for grazing), sneaking (moving stealthily).

• The passage is the famous Aesop's fable "The Boy Who Cried Wolf", whose moral is that a liar is not believed even when he speaks the truth.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Once, there was a boy who became bored when he watched over the village sheep (1)________ on the hillside. To entertain himself, he sang out, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers heard the cry, they came (2)________ the hill to drive the wolf away. But, when they arrived, they saw no wolf. The boy was amused when seeing their angry faces. “Don’t scream wolf, boy,” warned the villagers, “when there is no wolf!” They angrily went back down the hill. Later, the shepherd boy cried out once again, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers came, they saw there was no wolf, they said strictly, “Save your (3)________ cry for when there is really a wolf! Don’t cry ‘wolf’ when there is no wolf!” Later, the boy saw a real wolf sneaking around his flock. Alarmed, he jumped on his feet and cried out as loud as he could, “Wolf! Wolf!” But the villagers thought he was (4)________ them again, and so they didn’t come to help. At sunset, the villagers went looking for the boy who hadn’t returned with their sheep. When they went up the hill, they found him (5)________ as all the sheep were dead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. running up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The boy was on the hillside (at the top), and the villagers were below in the village. On hearing the cry of alarm they had to move upwards and quickly — hence "running up the hill".

◦ Correct: When the villagers heard the cry, they came running up the hill to drive the wolf away.

• The passage itself confirms the direction: after finding no wolf, "They angrily went back down the hill" and later "When they went up the hill, they found him ...".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "walking down" and 3 "running down" give the wrong direction — the villagers had to go up, not down.

• Option 1 "driving" does not combine with "came ... the hill" and is unsuitable for a village hillside emergency.

NOTE

• "Come/go + V-ing" is a common structure of movement: "came running", "went swimming", "came rushing".

• Prepositions/particles of direction: up (towards a higher place), down (towards a lower place), across, along, through, towards.

The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers heard the cry, they came (2)________ the hill to drive the wolf away. But, when they arrived, they saw no wolf. The boy was amused when seeing their angry faces. “Don’t scream wolf, boy,” warned the villagers, “when there is no wolf!” They angrily went back down the hill. Later, the shepherd boy cried out once again, “Wolf! Wolf! The wolf is chasing the sheep!” When the villagers came, they saw there was no wolf, they said strictly, “Save your (3)________ cry for when there is really a wolf! Don’t cry ‘wolf’ when there is no wolf!” Later, the boy saw a real wolf sneaking around his flock. Alarmed, he jumped on his feet and cried out as loud as he could, “Wolf! Wolf!” But the villagers thought he was (4)________ them again, and so they didn’t come to help. At sunset, the villagers went looking for the boy who hadn’t returned with their sheep. When they went up the hill, they found him (5)________ as all the sheep were dead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. frightened.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Frightened" means filled with fear; alarmed. A "frightened cry" is a cry of alarm — exactly the sort of cry that should be saved for a real emergency. (भयभीत)

◦ Correct: "Save your frightened cry for when there is really a wolf!"

• The villagers are scolding the boy for raising a false alarm, so they tell him to keep his cry of fear for a genuine danger.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Options 2 "laughable" and 3 "funny" suggest amusement — but a cry of "Wolf!" is meant to alarm, not amuse, and the villagers were angry, not entertained.

• Option 4 "muffled" means made quieter/deadened in sound, which contradicts a loud warning cry.

NOTE

• Note the participle pair: frightened (the feeling — a frightened boy) vs frightening (the cause — a frightening sound). The same rule applies to bored/boring, amused/amusing, excited/exciting, alarmed/alarming.

• Synonyms of frightened: scared, terrified, alarmed, petrified, panic-stricken.

When they went up the hill, they found him (5)________ as all the sheep were dead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. fooling.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Fooling (someone)" means deceiving or tricking someone; playing a joke on them. (मूर्ख बनाना / धोखा देना)

◦ Correct: But the villagers thought he was fooling them again, and so they didn't come to help.

• The word "again" is the clue — the boy had already tricked the villagers twice with a false alarm, so they assumed he was deceiving them once more.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "questioning" (asking questions) does not explain why they refused to help.

• Option 3 "fighting" is factually wrong — there was no quarrel, only a false alarm.

• Option 4 "seeing" gives no reason for their refusal to come.

NOTE

• Related expressions: "fool around" (to waste time), "make a fool of someone", "pull someone's leg", "take someone for a ride" (to cheat).

• Moral of the fable: Nobody believes a liar, even when he is telling the truth.

When they went up the hill, they found him (5)________ as all the sheep were dead.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. weeping.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Weeping" means crying; shedding tears out of sorrow. (रोना / विलाप करना)

◦ Correct: When they went up the hill, they found him weeping as all the sheep were dead.

• The clause "as all the sheep were dead" gives the reason, and the only emotionally consistent reaction to such a loss is weeping (grief).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "singing", 2 "happy" and 3 "dancing" all express joy, which directly contradicts the tragic outcome of the story.

• The conjunction "as" here means "because", so the second half of the sentence must explain a sad state.

NOTE

• Synonyms of weep: cry, sob, wail, lament, mourn, shed tears. Antonyms: rejoice, laugh, exult.

• "As" has three common uses: because (As it was raining, we stayed in), when/while (He sang as he walked) and comparison (as tall as his father).

question: What is the most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The no-confidence motion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "no-confidence motion" is the most powerful weapon available to Parliament for enforcing executive accountability. If a no-confidence motion is passed by a majority in the Lok Sabha, the entire Council of Ministers must resign. (अविश्वास प्रस्ताव)

• It flows from Article 75(3) of the Constitution, which lays down that the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• A no-confidence motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha, and it needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted.

• Other parliamentary devices of control are comparatively weaker: Question Hour, Zero Hour, adjournment motion, calling attention motion, censure motion, cut motions and the committee system.

• A censure motion differs from a no-confidence motion — it states reasons, may be moved against an individual minister, and its passage does not compel the government to resign.

NOTE

• India's first no-confidence motion was moved by Acharya J. B. Kripalani in 1963 against the Nehru government.

• The government of Morarji Desai (1979) and V. P. Singh (1990) fell after facing such motions; Atal Bihari Vajpayee's government lost a confidence vote by one vote in 1999.

question: Where is the Mahabodhi temple situated?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bodh Gaya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mahabodhi Temple" is situated at Bodh Gaya in the Gaya district of Bihar. It marks the spot where Gautama Buddha attained enlightenment (bodhi) under the Bodhi tree (a peepal tree). (महाबोधि मंदिर — बोधगया, बिहार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The temple was originally built by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE; the present brick structure dates largely from the 5th–6th century CE (Gupta period).

• It was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2002 and is one of the earliest surviving brick temples in India.

• The Mahabodhi Temple Act, 1949 governs its management.

NOTE

• The four principal Buddhist pilgrimage sites: Lumbini (birth, Nepal), Bodh Gaya (enlightenment, Bihar), Sarnath (first sermon, near Varanasi, UP) and Kushinagar (mahaparinirvana, UP).

• Other Buddhist sites in Bihar: Nalanda, Vikramshila, Rajgir (Griddhakuta hill) and Vaishali.

question: Which African leader wrote the autobiography ‘ Long Walk to Freedom’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Nelson Mandela.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Long Walk to Freedom" (published in 1994) is the autobiography of Nelson Mandela, the anti-apartheid revolutionary who became the first black President of South Africa (1994–1999). (नेल्सन मंडेला — लॉन्ग वॉक टू फ्रीडम)

• Much of the book was written secretly during his 27 years of imprisonment, largely on Robben Island.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Nelson Mandela was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1993 (jointly with F. W. de Klerk) and India's highest civilian honour, the Bharat Ratna, in 1990 — he was only the second foreigner to receive it after Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan.

• He was affectionately called "Madiba"; his birthday, 18 July, is observed as Nelson Mandela International Day by the UN.

• He was often described as the "Gandhi of South Africa" for his commitment to non-violent struggle.

NOTE

• Other options: Robert Mugabe (Zimbabwe), Muammar Gaddafi (Libya) and Archbishop Desmond Tutu (South Africa, Nobel Peace Prize 1984, chaired the Truth and Reconciliation Commission).

question: In which year was the Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM) scheme launched by Government of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1979.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Training of Rural Youth for Self Employment (TRYSEM)" scheme was launched by the Government of India in 1979 (on 15 August 1979). (ट्राइसेम — 1979)

• Its objective was to provide technical skills and training to rural youth (aged 18–35) from below-poverty-line families so that they could take up self-employment in agriculture, industry, services and business.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• TRYSEM operated as a sub-component of the Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP), which itself was launched in 1978–80.

• In 1999, TRYSEM was merged, along with IRDP, DWCRA, SITRA, GKY and MWS, into the single self-employment programme "Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)".

• SGSY was later restructured as the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM) / Aajeevika (2011), and skill training for rural youth now runs under DDU-GKY (2014).

NOTE

• Landmark rural development schemes for SSC: CDP (1952), IRDP (1978), TRYSEM (1979), JRY (1989), EAS (1993), PMGSY (2000), SGSY (1999), NREGA/MGNREGA (2005/2006), NRLM (2011), DDU-GKY (2014).

question: Under the Chief Minister Learn and Earn Scheme of Madhya Pradesh, the government will NOT provide which of the following?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Laptops.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Mukhyamantri Seekho–Kamao Yojana (Chief Minister Learn and Earn Scheme)" of Madhya Pradesh, launched in 2023, provides on-the-job training, employable skills and a monthly stipend (financial assistance) to educated unemployed youth. (मुख्यमंत्री सीखो-कमाओ योजना)

• The scheme does NOT provide laptops — laptop distribution is a separate state initiative for meritorious students.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Eligibility: youth of Madhya Pradesh aged 18–29 years, who have passed Class 12 / ITI / diploma / graduation or higher.

• Trainees receive a monthly stipend of roughly ₹8,000–₹10,000, of which 75% is paid by the state government and the rest by the establishment.

• Training is offered in about 700+ work areas, and trainees also get a certificate from the MP State Skill Development Board.

NOTE

• Comparable skilling schemes: PMKVY (Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, 2015), DDU-GKY (2014) for rural youth, and the National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme (NAPS).

question: Noted dance historian Dr. Sunil Kothari was awarded Madhabdev Award in 2019 by the Government of Assam for popularising which dance form of the state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Dr. Sunil Kothari, the noted dance historian, scholar and critic, was conferred the "Madhabdev Award" in 2019 by the Government of Assam for his outstanding contribution to popularising the Sattriya dance form of the state. (सत्रीय नृत्य — असम)

• Sattriya was introduced in the 15th century by the great Vaishnava saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardeva as a medium of devotional expression in the monasteries (sattras) of Assam.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sattriya was formally recognised as a classical dance form by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, becoming the eighth Indian classical dance.

• The Madhabdev Award is named after Madhavdeva, the chief disciple of Srimanta Sankardeva.

• Dr. Sunil Kothari was honoured with the Padma Shri (2001) and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1995).

NOTE

• The eight classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (Uttar Pradesh), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

• The other options are folk forms: Bihu (Assam's harvest dance), Bagurumba (Bodo tribe of Assam) and Ojapali (a narrative song-and-dance tradition of Assam).

question: What is the usual term used to describe the climate of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tropical monsoon.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The climate of India is usually described as the "tropical monsoon" type (in Koppen's scheme, "Amw" – tropical monsoon climate). The word "monsoon" comes from the Arabic "mausim", meaning season, and refers to the seasonal reversal of wind direction. (उष्णकटिबंधीय मानसूनी जलवायु)

• The Tropic of Cancer (23½°N) passes through the middle of the country, so India lies partly in the tropical and partly in the sub-tropical zone, but the overall character is monsoonal.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The four seasons recognised by the India Meteorological Department (IMD):

◦ Winter (December–February), Summer/Pre-monsoon (March–May), South-West Monsoon / rainy season (June–September) and Post-monsoon / retreating monsoon (October–November).

• The South-West monsoon gives India about 75% of its annual rainfall; it normally reaches Kerala around 1 June and withdraws by mid-September.

• Mawsynram and Cherrapunji (Sohra) in Meghalaya are among the wettest places on Earth, while Jaisalmer (Rajasthan) is among the driest.

NOTE

• The Himalayas act as a climatic divide, blocking the cold Central Asian winds, and the Western Ghats cause heavy orographic rainfall on their windward side with a rain-shadow area to their east.

question: Dandari (Dancing) troupes perform __________ during the festival of Diwali for a fortnight with participation from Kolam and Raj Gond tribes.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ghusadi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Ghusadi (Gusadi)" is the celebrated tribal dance performed by Dandari troupes during the Diwali festival for a fortnight, with participation from the Kolam and Raj Gond tribes. (घुसडी नृत्य)

• It is popular in the Adilabad district of Telangana and the adjoining Gond areas of Maharashtra. Male dancers wear headgear of peacock feathers, animal-skin garments, beards of goat hair and smear ash on their bodies.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kanaka Raju, a Gond tribal artist from Adilabad, was awarded the Padma Shri in 2021 for popularising the Gusadi dance.

• The Gonds are among the largest tribal groups in India, spread across Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra and Odisha.

NOTE

• The other options are also folk/tribal dances: Chhau (a masked martial dance of Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal — inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010), Baiga Pardhoni (a wedding dance of the Baiga tribe of Madhya Pradesh) and Rout Nacha (a cowherd community dance of Chhattisgarh performed at Diwali).

question: How many gold medals did India win at the ISSF Junior World Cup 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 6.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India won 6 gold medals at the ISSF Junior World Cup 2023, finishing on top of the medal tally. (आईएसएसएफ जूनियर विश्व कप 2023 — भारत को 6 स्वर्ण)

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) Junior World Cup is the premier global shooting competition for junior athletes, held in rifle, pistol and shotgun events.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The ISSF was founded in 1907 and has its headquarters at Munich, Germany.

• India has emerged as a shooting powerhouse at the junior level, regularly topping ISSF Junior World Championship and Junior World Cup medal tables.

• The National Rifle Association of India (NRAI), founded in 1951, is the governing body for shooting sport in India.

NOTE

• Indian shooting greats: Abhinav Bindra (India's first individual Olympic gold, 10 m air rifle, Beijing 2008), Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore (silver, Athens 2004), Gagan Narang, Vijay Kumar, Manu Bhaker and Saurabh Chaudhary.

question: _____________ is the first Indian woman to have won a Grammy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tanvi Shah.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Tanvi Shah is the first Indian woman to win a Grammy Award. She won it in 2010 for the song "Jai Ho" from the film *Slumdog Millionaire*, in the category Best Song Written for Motion Picture, Television or Other Visual Media. (तन्वी शाह — ग्रैमी जीतने वाली पहली भारतीय महिला)

• She wrote and sang the Spanish portions of the song, and shared the award with A. R. Rahman and lyricist Gulzar.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• At the 52nd Grammy Awards (2010), A. R. Rahman won two Grammys — Best Compilation Soundtrack Album and Best Song Written for Visual Media — for *Slumdog Millionaire*.

• Other Indian Grammy winners include Pandit Ravi Shankar (the first Indian, 1968), Zakir Hussain, Vishwa Mohan Bhatt, Ricky Kej and Falguni Shah (Falu).

NOTE

• The Grammy Awards are presented annually by the Recording Academy of the United States for outstanding achievement in the music industry; they began in 1959.

• The other options — Shalmali Kholgade, Palak Muchhal and Shilpa Rao — are well-known Indian playback singers but have not won a Grammy.

question: Which Indian musician personality’s native place is West Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bappi Lahiri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Bappi Lahiri (born Alokesh Lahiri, 1952–2022) hailed from Jalpaiguri in West Bengal. He was a celebrated music director, singer and composer who introduced disco music to Indian cinema. (बप्पी लहरी — पश्चिम बंगाल)

• He is remembered for chart-busting scores in films such as *Disco Dancer*, *Namak Halaal*, *Sharaabi*, *Himmatwala* and *Dance Dance*, and for his trademark gold jewellery.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Naushad Ali (1919–2006) was from Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh; he composed for *Baiju Bawra*, *Mughal-e-Azam* and received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (1981).

• O. P. Nayyar (1926–2007) was born in Lahore (undivided Punjab) and was famous for never using Lata Mangeshkar's voice.

• Ilaiyaraaja (born 1943) is from Tamil Nadu; he is a Padma Vibhushan awardee and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha.

NOTE

• Famous musicians from West Bengal: Rabindranath Tagore, Salil Chowdhury, S. D. Burman (born in Comilla, of the Tripura royal family, but long associated with Bengal), R. D. Burman, Hemanta Mukherjee, Manna Dey and Pandit Ravi Shankar.

question: According to the Census of India 2011, which State/Union Territory has the lowest sex ratio?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daman and Diu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Census of India 2011, the Union Territory of Daman and Diu recorded the lowest sex ratio among all States/UTs, at only 618 females per 1,000 males. (दमन और दीव — 618)

• The extremely low figure is explained mainly by heavy in-migration of male industrial workers into the UT's factories.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sex ratio in India (2011) = 943 females per 1,000 males (up from 933 in 2001).

• Kerala has the highest sex ratio (1,084), followed by Puducherry (1,037); among UTs the lowest after Daman and Diu are Dadra and Nagar Haveli (774) and Chandigarh (818).

• Among states, Haryana has the lowest sex ratio (879), followed by Jammu and Kashmir (889).

• The child sex ratio (0–6 years) in 2011 was 919, the lowest since Independence.

NOTE

• Census 2011 was the 15th national census and the 7th since Independence. Its motto was "Our Census, Our Future".

• Other Census 2011 facts: literacy rate 74.04% (Kerala highest at 93.91%, Bihar lowest at 61.80%); most populous state — Uttar Pradesh; least populous — Sikkim; highest density — Bihar (1,106/km²).

question: Which of the following is an autobiography of the famous cricketer Sourav Ganguly?
option_4: Memories of My Life and Times
solution_text:
The correct answer is A Century is not enough.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "A Century Is Not Enough" (2018), co-written with Gautam Bhattacharya, is the autobiography of the former Indian cricket captain Sourav Ganguly. (सौरव गांगुली की आत्मकथा)

• Nicknamed "Dada" and the "Prince of Kolkata", Ganguly captained India from 2000 to 2005 and is credited with rebuilding the team after the match-fixing crisis.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Sourav Ganguly served as President of the BCCI (2019–2022) and earlier as President of the Cricket Association of Bengal.

• He scored 131 on Test debut at Lord's (1996) and was one of the finest ODI batsmen of his generation, with over 11,000 ODI runs.

NOTE

• Matching the other titles: "A Shot at History" — Abhinav Bindra; "The Dream of Revolution" — a biography of Jayaprakash Narayan (by Bimal Prasad and Sujata Prasad); "Memories of My Life and Times" — Bipin Chandra Pal.

• Other cricket autobiographies: "Playing It My Way" (Sachin Tendulkar), "The Test of My Life" (Yuvraj Singh), "Straight from the Heart" (Kapil Dev), "Sunny Days" (Sunil Gavaskar).

question:
Consider the following statement about the Government of India Act, 1935.

1. This act was enacted by the British Parliament.

2. This Act was divided into two separate acts for India and Burma Government.

3. This act was commenced from the 1 April 1935.

Select the correct statement(s) using the code given below.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both 1 and 2.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Statement 1 is CORRECT — the Government of India Act, 1935 was passed/enacted by the British Parliament in August 1935. It was the longest Act ever enacted by the British Parliament up to that time (321 sections and 10 schedules). (भारत शासन अधिनियम, 1935)

• Statement 2 is CORRECT — the Act was later split into two separate Acts, namely the Government of India Act, 1935 and the Government of Burma Act, 1935, since Burma was separated from India in 1937.

• Statement 3 is INCORRECT — the Act did not commence on 1 April 1935. Its provincial provisions came into force on 1 April 1937, when provincial autonomy was introduced and elections were held in 1937.

• Hence only statements 1 and 2 are correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Main features of the GoI Act, 1935:

◦ Provided for an All-India Federation of provinces and princely states (this part never came into being).

◦ Abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy; introduced dyarchy at the Centre.

◦ Divided powers into three lists — Federal, Provincial and Concurrent — with residuary powers given to the Viceroy.

◦ Provided for a Federal Court (established 1937) and the Reserve Bank of India (1935).

◦ Extended separate electorates to depressed classes, women and labour.

NOTE

• The GoI Act, 1935 is often called the "blueprint of the Indian Constitution" — a large part of the Constitution of India (federal scheme, office of Governor, emergency provisions, public service commissions) is derived from it.

question: Who among the following established a unit of horsepower that is equal to one horse doing 33,000 foot - pounds of work in one minute?
solution_text:
The correct answer is James Watt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Scottish inventor and engineer James Watt (1736–1819) defined the unit "horsepower" as the work done by one horse equal to 33,000 foot-pounds of work per minute. (जेम्स वाट — अश्वशक्ति)

• He devised the unit to help market his improved steam engine by comparing its output with the draught horses it replaced.

• 1 horsepower (mechanical) = 33,000 ft·lb/min = 550 ft·lb/s ≈ 746 watts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The SI unit of power, the "watt (W)", is named in his honour. 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

• Watt's key contribution was the separate condenser (1765), which vastly improved the efficiency of the Newcomen steam engine and became a driving force of the Industrial Revolution.

NOTE

• Other "James" scientists in the options: James Croll (theory of ice ages and orbital forcing), James Dwight Dana (American geologist and mineralogist, author of *System of Mineralogy*), and Joseph Black (Scottish chemist known for latent heat, often confused with "James Black").

• Units named after scientists: newton (force), joule (energy), pascal (pressure), hertz (frequency), ampere (current), volt (potential difference), ohm (resistance).

question: In which year was the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act passed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1976.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act was passed in 1976, during the National Emergency (1975–77) under the government of Indira Gandhi. (42वाँ संविधान संशोधन अधिनियम — 1976)

• It is the most comprehensive amendment ever made and is popularly called the "Mini-Constitution" or the "Constitution of Indira".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Major changes made by the 42nd Amendment:

◦ Added the words "SOCIALIST", "SECULAR" and "INTEGRITY" to the Preamble.

◦ Added Part IV-A — Fundamental Duties (Article 51A), on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

◦ Added Article 39A (free legal aid), 43A (workers' participation) and 48A (protection of environment) to the Directive Principles.

◦ Transferred five subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List — education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice.

◦ Made the President bound by the advice of the Council of Ministers and extended the term of the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies from 5 to 6 years.

NOTE

• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978 (Janata Party government) reversed many of these changes — it restored the 5-year term, removed the Right to Property from Fundamental Rights (making it a legal right under Article 300A) and replaced "internal disturbance" with "armed rebellion" as a ground for National Emergency.

question: Who among the following leaders led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kunwar Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Babu Kunwar Singh (Veer Kunwar Singh), the zamindar of Jagdishpur in Shahabad (present-day Bhojpur district), Bihar, led the Revolt of 1857 in Bihar. (वीर कुंवर सिंह — बिहार, 1857)

• He was about 80 years old at the time of the revolt and is remembered for his brilliant guerrilla tactics against the British. He died in April 1858, shortly after a famous victory near Jagdishpur.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Leaders of the Revolt of 1857 at various centres:

◦ Delhi — Bahadur Shah Zafar / General Bakht Khan

◦ Kanpur — Nana Sahib and Tantia Tope

◦ Lucknow — Begum Hazrat Mahal

◦ Jhansi — Rani Lakshmibai

◦ Bareilly — Khan Bahadur Khan

◦ Faizabad — Maulvi Ahmadullah Shah

• The revolt began at Meerut on 10 May 1857, sparked by the greased cartridges of the Enfield rifle; Mangal Pandey of the 34th Native Infantry had already revolted at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857.

NOTE

• The other options belong to a much later period: Dr. Rajendra Prasad (first President of India) and Rajkumar Shukla (who persuaded Gandhiji to visit Champaran in 1917) were both from Bihar but of the 20th century.

• The revolt led to the Government of India Act, 1858, which ended Company rule and transferred power to the British Crown.

question: Shri Jagannathji Mela is held at _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Alwar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Shri Jagannathji Mela" is a well-known fair held at Alwar in Rajasthan. (श्री जगन्नाथजी मेला — अलवर, राजस्थान)

• It is celebrated with a grand rath yatra (chariot procession) of Lord Jagannath in the month of Ashadha (June–July) and attracts large crowds from the surrounding districts.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Alwar is part of Rajasthan's Mewat region and is famous for the Bala Qila (Alwar Fort), the City Palace, Siliserh Lake and the Sariska Tiger Reserve.

• Other important fairs of Rajasthan: Pushkar Fair (Ajmer — camel fair, Kartik Purnima), Urs of Khwaja Muinuddin Chishti (Ajmer), Teej Fair (Jaipur), Gangaur (Jaipur), Nagaur Cattle Fair, Baneshwar Fair (Dungarpur, the "tribal Kumbh") and Kolayat Fair (Bikaner).

NOTE

• The world-famous Jagannath Rath Yatra of Puri, Odisha, is a different, much larger festival; Cuttack and Sambalpur (Odisha) are known respectively for the Bali Yatra and the Sitalsasthi Carnival.

question: _____________ literally means 'dance of the enchantress'. It is one of the most striking in the Indian classical dance repertoire.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mohiniyattam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mohiniyattam" literally means the "dance of the enchantress" — from "Mohini", the enchanting female form taken by Lord Vishnu, and "attam", meaning dance. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

• It is a classical dance form of Kerala, performed solo by women, marked by gentle, swaying, lasya (graceful/feminine) movements resembling the swaying of palm trees.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Costume: a plain off-white (kasavu) sari with a gold border, with the hair tied in a bun on the left side and adorned with jasmine flowers.

• The dance is based on the Hastalakshanadeepika and follows the Natya Shastra; the accompanying music is in the Sopana style, sung in Manipravalam (a mix of Sanskrit and Malayalam).

• Kalyanikutty Amma is called the "mother of Mohiniyattam" for reviving it; the poet Vallathol Narayana Menon revived it through the Kerala Kalamandalam (1930).

NOTE

• Meanings of other classical dances: Kathakali (Kerala — "story-play", performed by men with elaborate make-up), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh — named after the village Kuchelapuram), Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu — Bha-Ra-Ta = bhava, raga, tala), Odissi (Odisha), Kathak (from "katha" — story), Manipuri and Sattriya.

question: The important milestones of the SHG Bank linkage movement was spearheaded by _______ with support from RBI.
solution_text:
The correct answer is NABARD.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The SHG (Self-Help Group) – Bank Linkage Programme was spearheaded by NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development) with the support of the Reserve Bank of India. (नाबार्ड — स्वयं सहायता समूह बैंक लिंकेज कार्यक्रम)

• It was launched as a pilot project in 1992 to link 500 SHGs with banks and has grown into the largest microfinance programme in the world in terms of outreach.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee, with its headquarters at Mumbai.

• Its functions include providing refinance to Regional Rural Banks, cooperative banks and other rural credit institutions, and supervising RRBs and cooperative banks.

• A Self-Help Group is a small voluntary association, usually of 10–20 women from a similar socio-economic background, that pools savings and gives small loans to members.

NOTE

• SEBI (1988/1992) regulates the securities market, not rural credit.

• Related institutions: RBI (central bank, 1935), SIDBI (small industries, 1990), EXIM Bank (1982), NHB (National Housing Bank, 1988).

• The National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM/Aajeevika) also works through SHGs for poverty alleviation.

question: Narendra Modi Cricket Stadium is one of the premier stadiums in India located at __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Narendra Modi Stadium" is located at Motera in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, on the banks of the Sabarmati river. (नरेंद्र मोदी स्टेडियम — अहमदाबाद)

• With a seating capacity of about 1,32,000, it is the largest cricket stadium in the world. It was rebuilt and inaugurated in February 2021, and forms part of the Sardar Patel Sports Enclave.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The stadium hosted the final of the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 (19 November 2023), in which Australia defeated India to win their sixth title.

• It is managed by the Gujarat Cricket Association and was designed by the Australian firm Populous.

• It also hosted the "Namaste Trump" event in February 2020.

NOTE

• Other major Indian cricket stadiums: Eden Gardens (Kolkata — the oldest, 1864), Wankhede Stadium (Mumbai), Arun Jaitley Stadium (Delhi, formerly Feroz Shah Kotla), M. A. Chidambaram Stadium (Chennai), M. Chinnaswamy Stadium (Bengaluru) and the Rajiv Gandhi International Stadium (Hyderabad).

question: The pre-monsoon showers are known as ________ in Kerala and Karnataka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is mango showers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The pre-monsoon showers that occur in Kerala and coastal Karnataka during April–May are known as "mango showers", because they help in the early ripening of mangoes. (आम्र वर्षा / मैंगो शावर)

• They are caused by local convectional thunderstorms in the hot summer months before the arrival of the South-West monsoon.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Regional names of local storms and pre-monsoon showers in India:

◦ Blossom shower / Cherry blossom — Karnataka, helps coffee flowers to bloom.

◦ Kalbaisakhi (Nor'westers) — West Bengal, Assam and Bihar; violent evening thunderstorms of Baisakh, also called "Bordoisila" in Assam.

◦ Loo — hot, dry, dust-laden wind of the northern plains in May–June.

◦ Mango shower — Kerala and coastal Karnataka.

NOTE

• Kalbaisakhi showers are beneficial for tea, jute and rice in eastern India.

• The South-West monsoon normally sets in over Kerala around 1 June and covers the whole country by mid-July; its withdrawal begins in September from north-west India.

question: Insufficient levels of parathyroid hormone and low amount of calcium in the blood causes which of the following conditions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hypocalcemia.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Hypocalcemia" is the condition of an abnormally low level of calcium in the blood. It results when the parathyroid glands secrete insufficient parathyroid hormone (PTH) — a state called hypoparathyroidism. (रक्त में कैल्शियम की कमी)

• PTH is the main regulator of calcium and phosphorus in the body: it raises blood calcium by releasing it from bones, increasing absorption in the intestine and reducing loss through the kidneys.

• Symptoms include muscle cramps, tetany, numbness and tingling (paraesthesia) and, in severe cases, convulsions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The opposite condition, hypercalcemia (excess calcium), results from hyperparathyroidism and can cause kidney stones and bone weakening.

• The parathyroid glands are four small glands located behind the thyroid gland in the neck.

• Calcitonin, secreted by the thyroid, has the opposite effect to PTH — it lowers blood calcium.

NOTE

• Other endocrine facts for SSC: Pituitary — "master gland"; Thyroxine deficiency causes goitre/cretinism; Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus; Adrenaline is the "emergency/fight-or-flight hormone".

• The other options are unrelated: Malaria is caused by the *Plasmodium* parasite spread by the female *Anopheles* mosquito; Anaemia is a deficiency of haemoglobin/red blood cells (often due to iron deficiency).

question: Team Rest of India won Irani Cup in 2023. Irani Cup was hosted in which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Irani Cup 2023 was hosted in Madhya Pradesh, at the Holkar Stadium, Indore, in March 2023. Rest of India defeated the Ranji Trophy champions Madhya Pradesh to lift the trophy. (ईरानी कप 2023 — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Irani Cup (started in 1959–60) is played annually between the Ranji Trophy winning team and a Rest of India side. It is named after Z. R. Irani, a long-serving member of the BCCI.

• Rest of India has won the Irani Cup the maximum number of times.

• Madhya Pradesh had won the Ranji Trophy 2021–22 under captain Aditya Shrivastava and coach Chandrakant Pandit, beating Mumbai in the final.

NOTE

• Major domestic cricket tournaments in India: Ranji Trophy (first-class, since 1934–35), Duleep Trophy (zonal, 1961–62), Irani Cup (1959–60), Vijay Hazare Trophy (one-day), Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20) and the Deodhar Trophy.

question: What is a dimension related to the sustainability of microfinance institutions in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Dependency on donor funding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Sustainability of a Microfinance Institution (MFI) means its ability to cover its costs from its own operations and continue functioning in the long run without outside support.

• Therefore, "dependency on donor funding" (grants, subsidies and soft loans from donors) is the key dimension of sustainability — the greater the dependence on donors, the less sustainable the institution, because such funding is uncertain and temporary. (दानदाता निधि पर निर्भरता)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Sustainability of MFIs is usually assessed on two levels:

◦ Operational Self-Sufficiency (OSS) — whether operating income covers operating costs, loan losses and financing costs.

◦ Financial Self-Sufficiency (FSS) — whether income covers all costs after adjusting for subsidies and inflation.

• Other dimensions include outreach (breadth and depth), repayment/recovery rate, operating efficiency and portfolio quality.

NOTE

• Microfinance provides small loans, savings and insurance to low-income households without collateral. The concept was pioneered by Prof. Muhammad Yunus through the Grameen Bank of Bangladesh (Nobel Peace Prize, 2006).

• In India, microfinance operates mainly through the SHG–Bank Linkage model (NABARD) and the MFI (JLG) model; NBFC-MFIs are regulated by the RBI, and the Malegam Committee (2011) framed key recommendations after the Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis.
